title: Adaptive summary strip + keyboard frequency mode for dense time-series
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: High-density timeseries cause legend overflow, slow hover tooltips, and poor keyboard discoverability for visually-impaired users.

Proposal: Introduce an adaptive summary strip — a condensed, inline aggregation layer that sits above the main time-series viewport. The summary strip should compute and visually surface per-viewport aggregates (min, max, median, last) at a coarse granularity and progressively refine when the user zooms or moves the focus.

Add a complementary "Keyboard Frequency Mode": a focused keyboard-first interaction that lets users step through aggregation tiers (coarse → medium → fine) and cycle between series using arrow keys. The mode emphasizes single-line, high-contrast text summaries announced to assistive tech and avoids frequent ARIA updates by batching announcements.

Goals: Improve legibility of dense charts at-a-glance, reduce legend clutter, maintain 60fps for pan/zoom on typical laptop GPUs, and make keyboard + screenreader interactions predictable and performant.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive summary strip renders a 1-line aggregation summary for current viewport and updates on pan/zoom within 120ms on sample dataset (1M points, server-side aggregated)
Keyboard Frequency Mode allows stepping between 3 aggregation tiers via keyboard and announces a concise summary to screen readers no more than once per 350ms
Legend collapse behavior: when series > 6, auto-collapse low-visibility series into a "More" group with keyboard-accessible expand/collapse
Tooltip hover latency < 50ms for sampled points on 100k-series view (desktop Chrome), and gracefully degrades to static summary on mobile to preserve responsiveness
Design tokens required (spacing, tokenColor/alpha, compact-typeface, contrast ramp) defined and added to the design system package
Visual QA for contrast ratios: summary text >= 4.5:1 against background and >= 3:1 for secondary elements
Docs: design spec, keyboard interaction matrix, and a11y notes published in Confluence with code examples and links to demo harness

comments: 2026-02-28 — Asha Patel: Initial spike complete. Strips + stacked micro-sparklines both viable. Strips win for single-line density and keyboard focus. Attached initial mock links.

2026-03-03 — Miguel Ortega: Built Storybook prototype for strip + keyboard stepping. Observed jank when drawing unthrottled updates at 1M points; will propose offscreen canvas + sample-on-update approach. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/charts/pull/1821

2026-03-05 — Maya Chen (a11y): Reviewed ARIA plan. Recommend live region batching and a mode toggle to avoid noisy announcements. Flag: ensure focus management when expanding 'More' group to stay within chart tab order.

2026-03-07 — PM review (Lena Hofstad): Agree on strip approach. Request a fallback summary-line for mobile with simplified metrics (min/last). Please add e2e tests that assert keyboard traversal order.

2026-03-09 — Engineering (ENG-18723): Prototype uses prefix KV-caching for aggregates and a worker-based resampling pipeline. Measured interactive pan latency ~95ms before optimizations; target is <120ms for coarse updates and <40ms for refined on local caches.
